newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 26.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 26. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet told governors from all over Indonesia the general election was not engineered to defend the status quo.
West Kalimantan Governor Aspar Aswin said the provincial capital Pontianak had returned to normal and residents had resumed daily activities after recent ethnic violence.

Political observers have backed comments by the Catholic church that it is not a sin to abstain from voting at the general election as it is every citizen's basic right and people breach no law if they do not exercise it.

Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo says Indonesia's textile quota is good enough and does not have a connection with the current embargoes placed upon some Indonesian textile imports by the European Union.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet has told governors from all of Indonesia's provinces to examine the impact on small traders before approving the building of supermarkets, particularly in small towns.
